Definition: of Hebrew origin (H3110); Joannes (i.e. Jochanan), the name of four Israelites:--John.
BiblicalUsage: John is the name of the Baptist who prepared the way and the apostle who leaned on Jesus' breast. In Matthew 3:1 John the Baptist comes preaching in the wilderness of Judea, in John 1:6 there is a man sent from God, whose name is John, and in Acts 3:1 Peter and John go up together to the temple at the hour of prayer.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the two Johns show two kinds of faithfulness: one cried in the wilderness and lost his head, and the other stayed beside Jesus to the end and wrote it all down.
RelatedPeople: John the Baptist; John the Apostle; Simon Peter
